text:
Matthew Robertson is a 25-year-old Edmonton native and 2019 second-round pick who got back into the Rangers' lineup on Nov 7 and played four straight on the road trip, including what Forever Blueshirts called an impressive homecoming in Edmonton. The same outlet thinks he'll keep his spot over Scott Morrow when the defense is healthy.

Four games is too few to judge. He's played about 13 minutes a night with no points, and the Rangers have taken 55% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, a little better than without him. Last season, in 72 games, he had 18 points, and Evolving-Hockey had him as a middle-of-the-pack defenseman, 88th of 215.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking names the concern: only 24% of his exits keep possession, so watch for clears off the glass when the forecheck comes. History is cautious about players picked where he was, with 36 of the 115 defensemen taken 39th to 59th since 2005 (with four-plus seasons) reaching 200 NHL games. Our talent range has him around 11 points if he stays in. The competition with Morrow is the thing to watch.
